items.question: What kind of body of water was the sail training ship Oliver Hazard Perry sitting in when seawater got into its machinery spaces at Newport?
items.expected_answer: It was in a harbor (moored at the Fort Adams State Park dock in Newport, Rhode Island).

evidence.quote: Waterway information Harbor Figure 2. Area where the engine room flooding occurred aboard the Oliver Hazard Perry as indicated by a circled X. (Background source: Google Maps) Engine Room Flooding aboard Sailing School Vessel Oliver Hazard Perry MIR-26-09 3 1 Factual Information 1.1 Background The 128-foot-long, steel-hulled, three-masted, square-rigged tall ship Oliver Hazard Perry was certified by the US Coast Guard under Title 46 Code of Federal Regulations Subchapter R as a sailing school vessel.

items.notes: Tests retrieval of the waterway-type field at the end of the casualty summary table, whose chunk boundary falls before the background section (the boundary is only a figure caption and page header, so the passage reads awkwardly).

items.question: How many years of experience did the bosun aboard the Oliver Hazard Perry have when he discovered the engine room flooding in Newport?
items.expected_answer: The report does not state the bosun's years of experience.
items.notes: Tests that the system declines to invent crew experience details; the report only says the bosun was familiar with the bilge system.
